name: Red Hill South
intro: Red Hill South is the lower, quieter half of the Red Hill plateau, and for visitors who already know the headline village it is often the better stay. The roads drop down off the ridge into a softer landscape  -  a community shop, a small handful of cellar doors, a popular country pub, and a long catalogue of bed-and-breakfasts in renovated farmhouses. The cellar doors here  -  Foxeys Hangout, Quealy, Lindenderry  -  pull a different crowd to the ridge-top names, and the lunch options below Red Hill village proper are some of the most rewarding on the Peninsula. The Red Hill Market on the first Saturday of the month sits between the two villages and is genuinely the best market on the Peninsula. Stay here when the upper village is full or when you want a cellar-door weekend that is slightly off the obvious circuit.
factualLede: Red Hill South is a quiet rural locality on the lower Red Hill plateau on the Mornington Peninsula, 85 km from Melbourne, with a country pub, established cellar doors and a high concentration of farmhouse bed-and-breakfasts.

heroImage.alt: Vines and a farmhouse gate at Red Hill South in early autumn light

tldr: Red Hill South is the lower-elevation half of the Red Hill plateau — same wine country, quieter roads, more bed-and-breakfasts than its better-known neighbour.
Best for: returning Peninsula visitors who already know Red Hill; couples on a B&B weekend; market shoppers.
Signature experience: Red Hill Market on a first Saturday morning, then a long lunch at one of the lower cellar doors.
A weekend; two nights minimum to see the cellar doors properly.
Less foot traffic than Red Hill village proper — book the cellar doors but you will not be queuing.
notFor: first-time visitors who haven't seen Red Hill village
signature: The quieter, lower-elevation half of the Peninsula's wine country — better B&Bs, fewer crowds, the same cellar-door belt.
skip: Driving past the country pub assuming it's nothing — it's a serious lunch destination most weekends.
bestDay: Red Hill Market on a first Saturday morning, late lunch at a lower-cellar-door restaurant, afternoon flight at a second cellar door, dinner held loosely at the pub.
insiderNote: Stay at a Red Hill South farmhouse B&B and walk to a cellar door for the wine-country weekend the brochures keep promising.
